🎯 Today’s objective

By the end of this lesson I can...

✓ I can continue sequences and find the term-to-term rule

✓ I can find and use the nth term

✓ I can decide if a number is in a sequence

So you can predict how viral your video will go!

Calculator

[5 marks]

Sequence A has nth term 5n + 3. Sequence B has nth term 80 − 2n. Find the value of n for which the two sequences have the same term, and find that term.

Hint

Answer

5n + 3 = 80 − 2n.

Answer: n = 11; 58

Q2

Calculator

[5 marks]

Mo saves £15 in week 1, £20 in week 2, £25 in week 3, and so on. (a) Write the nth term for the amount saved in week n. (b) In which week does he first save more than £100?

Hint

Answer

nth term, then an inequality.

Answer: Week 19

Hint

Answer

The gap is 0.4 each week.

Answer: 0.4n + 2.6; week 19

Hard 2: mixed

Q1

Calculator

[6 marks]

Tables are put in a row. 1 table seats 6, 2 tables seat 10, 3 tables seat 14. (a) Write the nth term. (b) 72 people come to a party. How many tables are needed? (c) Tables cost £8.50 each to hire. Find the cost.

Hint

Answer

Each table adds 4 seats.

Answer: 4n + 2; 18 tables; £153.00

click to solve →

Q2

Calculator

[6 marks]

A sequence has nth term 4n + 3. (a) Explain why every term is odd. (b) Is 99 a term of the sequence? If so, which term?

Hint

Answer

4n is always even.

Answer: Always odd; 99 is the 24th term

click to solve →

Q3

Calculator

[6 marks]

Patterns are made from matchsticks. Pattern 1 uses 4 matches, pattern 2 uses 7, pattern 3 uses 10 and pattern 4 uses 13. (a) Find the nth term. (b) Is there a pattern that uses exactly 100 matches? (c) Kim has 250 matches. What is the biggest pattern number she can make?

Hint

Answer

Each pattern adds 3 matches.

Answer: 3n + 1; yes, pattern 33; pattern 83
